title: The ZIP-LT Study: Effect of Liver Transplantation on Intestinal Permeability in Patients with Stable Liver Graft Function
summary:
Background and Objectives
Impaired intestinal permeability (“leaky gut”) promotes bacterial translocation and increases the risk of infection in patients with liver disease. After liver transplantation, the intestinal barrier appears to largely normalize when graft function is stable. However, it remains unclear whether intestinal permeability differs between patients with stable and unstable graft function and how it correlates with immunological changes and clinical parameters. The aim of the ZIP-LT study is to compare intestinal permeability between liver transplant recipients and healthy controls and to investigate correlations with immunological and clinical parameters.
Methods:
In this prospective, single-center, cross-sectional study, three groups of 21 participants each will be examined. During a single outpatient study visit, intestinal permeability will be determined using a multisugar test. In addition, blood samples will be collected for the analysis of intestinal barrier biomarkers and immunological parameters, and clinical data will be recorded.
Endpoints:
Differences in intestinal permeability between patients with stable and unstable liver graft function, measured using the lactulose/rhamnose ratio (L/R) in the multisugar test.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group 1: Patients after LTx with stable long-term graft function: all criteria must be met:
a) Age ≥ 18 years
b) Status following orthotopic liver transplantation 
c) Liver transplantation ≥ 3 years
d) No acute rejection in the past 12 months (histologically confirmed or treated with
a corticosteroid equivalent >20 mg/day)
e) VCTE-LSM (Fibroscan) ≤ 10 kPa in the past 12 months; if unavailable: FIB4 score ≤ 3.25
f) Stable immunosuppression in the past 12 months (A switch within the same drug class—e.g., switching between calcineurin inhibitors—is permitted. Not permitted are intensification via higher target levels, the addition of another immunosuppressive agent, or switching from mycophenolate mofetil to everolimus)

Group 2: Patients after LTx without stable long-term graft function:
a) Age ≥ 18 years
b)  Status following orthotopic liver transplantation
c) At least 1 of the following criteria must be met:
1.  Liver transplantation <3 years ago
2. Acute rejection within the last 12 months (histologically confirmed or treated with
a corticosteroid equivalent >20 mg/day)
3.  VCTE-LSM (Fibroscan) >10 kPa within the last 12 months; if unavailable: FIB4 score > 3.25
4. Intensification of  immunosuppression within the last 12 months (higher target levels, addition of another immunosuppressive agent, or switch from mycophenolate mofetil to everolimus)

Group 3: Controls without liver disease:
Inclusion criteria for the control group:
a) Age ≥ 18 years
b) No known acute or chronic liver disease
c) No known gastrointestinal disease
d) No history of organ transplantation
e) No use of immunomodulators or immunosuppressants
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion Criteria
a) Gastrointestinal disease: IBD (Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis), celiac disease, acute gastroenteritis, chronic diarrhea
b) Primary sclerosing cholangitis
c) Pregnancy or breastfeeding
d) Hypersensitivity or allergies to sucrose, rhamnose, sucralose, erythritol, or lactulose
e) Hereditary fructose intolerance
f) Lactulose treatment within the last 48 hours
g) Malignancies undergoing systemic therapy, such as chemotherapy or radiation therapy
